I recall a particularly challenging project where I had to optimize our ETL pipelines, which were slowing down our data warehouse. We were using dbt for our analytics engineering, and our SQL queries were riddled with anti-patterns that were killing pipeline performance.

The problem was that our daily record count had grown to over 500 million, and our ETL jobs were taking hours to complete. We were using AWS Redshift as our data warehouse, and our dbt models were using inefficient SQL joins and subqueries.

To tackle this, I implemented a few key changes. I refactored our dbt models to use more efficient SQL queries, such as replacing correlated subqueries with window functions and optimizing our join orders. I also worked with our data team to implement a data warehousing best practice - using Redshift's Spectrum for external table queries.

The result was a 40% reduction in ETL runtime, which not only improved our data freshness but also reduced our compute costs. I was proud to have led this effort, and it was a great example of how optimizing SQL queries can have a significant impact on pipeline performance.
